rationale: Record linking rather than a new claim: the parent configuration question's account lists voter-adding changes and their consequences as witnessed by the child question, but its execution set only names its own two receipts. This update adds the child's two decisive receipts to that set (b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 for the five-voter configuration loss and a608e5f60ae4415981c1024522a24a0d for the post-heal log disagreement) with joint history explaining that they are complete executions of the child scenario cited here only for the consequence named in the parent's limitations, and rescopes the parent's own limitation so it no longer claims no divergence was witnessed in any execution. No comparison, execution index, counterevidence item or witness value changes.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: In this scenario and window no acknowledged entry was lost after healing: two seconds after the partition healed, the isolated node and the majority-side leader each still held their own acknowledged entry in their own log store, neither had applied an entry absent from its own log, and the flag-off control's isolated side never acknowledged an entry.
knowledge.conditions: Five-voter committed configuration with a three-voter snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the restarted node isolated with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns and both sides acknowledging a distinct client write; two second apply timeout and two second heal settle; in-memory log stores.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: The parent question is answered by receipt 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 (exit 0, six events, no parse loss) with receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 as the earlier execution of the same declaration: with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, the restarted node reported after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored (violated at witness event index 1 against the admission at index 0 recording before_latest_index 1 with one server), and the flag-off control kept index 1 with one voter (evaluated event index 3). The snapshot-present case in the same receipt shows the loss with a committed membership change newer than the snapshot (violated at witness index 5, admission 4). Mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration and the startup log scan (api.go:604-620) is the only other, but restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped; processLogs forwards them to the FSM without ever updating r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The child question has since witnessed the multi-voter variant and its consequences: with a five-voter committed configuration and a three-voter snapshot the restarted node came back at index 1 with three servers (receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, violated at witness index 15, control 18), and after a heal the two sides held different entries at the same log index (receipt a608e5f60ae4415981c1024522a24a0d, violated at witness index 27, control 29), while the two-second window (receipt 4e9eaa72cf594018b8414a8d8efb7cb3) is a negative for loss of an acknowledged entry.
counterevidence: The flag-off controls keep the committed configuration in every cited execution, isolating the recovery path rather than the restart, the stores or the applied entries.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of its configuration index, which is why the snapshot-present case needed a configuration change newer than the snapshot.
limitations: The parent's own witness uses a single-voter configuration and a nonvoter addition; voter-adding changes, minority leadership and the post-heal log disagreement are witnessed under the child question and are not observed in the parent's own executions.

No lost acknowledged entry is witnessed anywhere in this run: the child's two-second window is a negative for loss and its eight-second window shows the two logs disagreeing at one index rather than an entry disappearing.
The startup-blocking and authority questions are separate and are not part of this account.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipts 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 and 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 are the parent's own executions of the single-voter scenario, the second being the earlier execution of the same declaration before identity fields were corrected. Receipts b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, a608e5f60ae4415981c1024522a24a0d and 4e9eaa72cf594018b8414a8d8efb7cb3 belong to the child multi-voter question (five voters grown from three after a deliberate snapshot, isolation of the restarted node with one committed voter) and are cited here only for the follow-on consequences named in the limitations. All five are complete executions over their own stores and sizes; the parent receipts agree with each other and the child receipts agree with each other on the configuration values they report, and none is a fragment of another.

experiment.revision_reason: The heal settle is extended from two to eight seconds so a losing suffix has time to be truncated, and the event now carries logs_differ_at_conflict_index, which compares the two nodes' log entries at the index where the isolated side wrote. Scenario, isolation, waits and the two-sided apply are unchanged.

scope.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot predating the membership change, isolated with one committed voter immediately after the restart; both sides acknowledge a distinct client write, the partition heals, and after eight seconds the event reports whether the two nodes' logs hold different entries at the same index, whether either node applied an entry absent from its own log, and the leadership and acknowledgement outcomes. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: A successful Apply is an acknowledgement to the client.
Two nodes holding different entries at the same log index after healing is a violation of log agreement.
Eight seconds is enough for AppendEntries exchange between the two sides.
excluded: Entry contents at the conflict index, which the probe reports as empty strings.
Any claim about durable stores; the in-memory stores are used.

experiment.prefix: The harness reuses the multi-voter scenario construction and the two-sided apply, then scans each side's log store for its own acknowledged entry, compares the two nodes' entries at the isolated side's last index, and emits logs_differ_at_conflict_index with the per-side log and FSM survival flags, the applied-without-log operands, and the leadership and acknowledgement outcomes. No production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns log agreement: after a partition heals, two replicas of the committed configuration must not hold different entries at the same index, especially when both writes were acknowledged to clients.

comparisons.description: After healing, the two nodes must agree at the index where the isolated side wrote; the defect prediction is that they hold different entries there.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side never writes, so the two logs cannot differ at that index.
